statement: Kai builds a cube wall 5 long, 3 tall and 2 thick. He removes an archway 1 cube wide and 2 tall from the middle of the bottom, right through. How many cubes are left?

choices.misconception: I only counted the front layer that I could picture, 15 cubes, and took away its 2 archway cubes.
I only counted the front layer of the wall and forgot the archway too.
I took away 4 cubes from the front layer and 4 from the back layer, but each layer only loses 2.
I only took the archway out of the front layer, but it goes right through, so the back layer loses 2 cubes as well.

hints: How many cubes does the whole wall have before the archway?
Count the full block as length times height times thickness. Then count the cubes removed: the archway goes through every layer of the thickness, not just the one you can see.
The full wall has $5 \times 3 \times 2 = 30$ cubes. The archway removes 2 cubes from the front layer and 2 from the back layer.

solutions.reliable: The full wall is $5 \times 3 = 15$ cubes in each layer, and there are 2 layers, so 30 cubes. The archway is 1 cube wide and 2 cubes tall, so it takes 2 cubes out of each layer. It goes right through, so both layers lose 2: that is 4 cubes. $30 - 4 = 26$. The transferable idea: count a solid layer by layer, including the layers you cannot see.
solutions.elegant: Each layer becomes $15 - 2 = 13$ cubes, and there are 2 identical layers: $2 \times 13 = 26$.

whyOnTest: It checks that the student counts the hidden back layer of a solid, not just the face they can picture.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
